tagline: A former county road winds through forest to Yankee Springs’ lakes
intro: M-179 crosses forest land between U.S. 131 at Bradley and M-43 west of Hastings. The road bends past Sager Lake, passes north of Gun Lake and winds through Yankee Springs State Recreation Area. MDOT designated it the Chief Noonday Trail Recreational Heritage Route, now a Pure Michigan Byway, for its natural beauty and access to recreation. Its full length is 16.963 miles.

The name honors Noahquageshik, known as Chief Noonday, a leader of the Grand River Band of Ottawa Nation. He spent much of his life in what became Yankee Springs Township. The numbered highway is much newer: on October 1, 1998, the state took over the section of county road A-42 between U.S. 131 and M-43, assigning M-179 the following year. The landscape had changed too: by the 1930s, farming had depleted and eroded land at Yankee Springs. Federal acquisition and Civilian Conservation Corps reforestation preceded its transfer to Michigan in 1943.

Drive east from Bradley along 129th Avenue through rural eastern Allegan County. Across the Barry County line, the local name becomes Chief Noonday Road. After Yankee Springs, woodland continues along the road, which curves slightly north before turning east to its M-43 junction.

moments.title: Bradley
moments.text: A plank road helped bring Bradley into being in 1854. The community lies just east of U.S. 131’s exit 61. M-179 begins at the interchange west of Bradley and runs through the community before bending along Sager Lake’s southern edge. Farther east, it continues as 129th Avenue through rural forest in Allegan County.

moments.title: Gun Lake
moments.text: Gun Lake’s two halves are somewhat symmetrical, shaped like butterfly wings. Most of the lake lies in Barry County, with its southwestern tip extending into Allegan County. Yankee Springs Recreation Area occupies the northeastern shore, while summer homes, cottages and permanent residences line much of the lake. M-179 passes to the north. The lake drains into the Gun River, whose waters reach Lake Michigan through the Kalamazoo River. Gun Lake is the largest of the recreation area’s nine lakes. The recreation area provides boating and swimming on its lakes.

moments.title: Yankee Springs Recreation Area
moments.text: Glacial terrain and twentieth-century reforestation both shape Yankee Springs Recreation Area. By the 1930s, farming had left the soil eroded and depleted; the federal government acquired the land, and the Civilian Conservation Corps began replanting it. Michigan took over in 1943, adding it to the state park system. The recreation area covers 5,200 acres and includes nine lakes. Its features include the glacially carved kettle called Devil’s Soupbowl, Graves Hill Scenic Overlook and CCC-era buildings. M-179 winds through the recreation area before continuing east through woodland. Six miles of the North Country Trail pass through the park.
